plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: A herbaceous perennial producing large, fragrant, bowl-shaped to fully double blooms atop sturdy stems with deeply lobed glossy green foliage. A classic cottage garden favorite that can live for decades.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May-June in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Siberia, Mongolia, and northern China; widely cultivated in temperate gardens across North America, Europe, and Asia
plants.funFact: Peonies are often visited by ants, which feed on nectar on the flower buds; contrary to popular myth, the ants are not needed for the buds to open.

plants.name: Rosa gallica
plants.description: A deciduous shrub with fragrant, semi-double to double flowers in rich shades of crimson to pink, forming suckering thickets. One of the oldest cultivated roses, ancestral to many garden roses.
plants.location: Native to central and southern Europe and western Asia; cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Rosa gallica 'Officinalis', the Apothecary's Rose, was used in medieval medicine and its petals retain fragrance even when dried.

plants.name: Leucanthemum vulgare
plants.description: A hardy perennial wildflower with white ray petals around a bright yellow center, growing in meadows, roadsides, and grasslands. It forms clumps of dark green, spoon-shaped basal leaves.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to late summer (peaking late May through June)
plants.location: Native to Europe and temperate Asia; naturalized across North America, Australia, and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Its flower heads track the sun in the morning, and a single plant can produce up to 26,000 seeds in a season.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall, fast-growing tree with fern-like foliage that bursts into clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers, often carpeting the ground beneath. In the Northern Hemisphere subtropics it blooms in late spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Northern Hemisphere (May-June); October-November in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); planted in Mediterranean, Californian, Mexican, South African, and Australian cities
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, known as the 'Jacaranda City,' tens of thousands of trees line the streets, and in Mexico City the blooms arrive in spring.
